## **Extension of the Australian Apprenticeship Support Services**

The Australian Government has extended the Australian Apprenticeship Support Services for a further two-year period from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2028. More information can be found [here.](https://www.apprenticeships.gov.au/who-to-contact/Extension-of-the-Australian-Apprenticeship-Support-Services)

# Financial support for apprentices

Know what financial support you could be eligible for as an apprentice.

As an Australian Apprentice, you may be eligible for financial and non-financial support from the Australian Government and your State or Territory Government. The easiest way to check what support you may be eligible for is to check the [Apprenticeships Incentives Explorer](https://www.apprenticeships.gov.au/support-and-resources/incentives-explorer) or speak to your [Apprentice Connect Australia Provider](https://www.apprenticeships.gov.au/about-apprenticeships/apprentice-connect-australia-provider).

## Key Apprenticeship Program Apprentice Incentive

If you’re training as an Australian Apprentice in the clean energy or housing construction sectors, you may be eligible for support through the Key Apprenticeship Program (KAP) Apprentice Incentive.

KAP Apprentice Incentive provides financial support to eligible apprentices of up to $10,000 for full-time apprentices and up to $5,000 for part-time apprentices and paid in instalments below:

- $2,000 at 6, 12, 24 and 36 months and on completion for full-time apprentices
- $1,000 at 6, 12, 24 and 36 months and on completion for part-time apprentices

## Australian Apprentice Training Support Payment

If you’re training in a priority occupation listed on the [Australian Apprenticeship Priority Listarrow\_outwardOpens in new window or tab](https://www.dewr.gov.au/australian-apprenticeships/apprenticeship-support#toc-australian-apprenticeship-priority-list) you may be eligible to receive the Australian Apprentice Training Support Payment (AATSP). This payment of up to $2,500 is designed to help you with cost-of-living pressures and encourage you to complete your apprenticeship.

This payment is front loaded and paid in four instalments after you start your training.

- $625 at 6, 12, 18 and 24 months for full-time apprentices
- $315 at 6 and 12 months and $310 at 18 and 24 months for part-time apprentices

#### Am I eligible?

The [Australian Apprenticeships Incentive System Guidelinesarrow\_outwardOpens in new window or tab](https://www.dewr.gov.au/skills-support-individuals/resources/australian-apprenticeships-incentive-system-guidelines) outline the detailed eligibility for The Australian Apprentice Training Support Payment and the Key Apprenticeship Program Apprentice Incentive.

Your [Apprentice Connect Australia Provider](https://www.apprenticeships.gov.au/who-to-contact/search-for-a-provider) is also able to advise you on your eligibility and can help you to lodge a claim in the [Apprenticeships Data Management Systemarrow\_outwardOpens in new window or tab](https://adms.australianapprenticeships.gov.au/adms/sign-in).

## Australian Apprenticeship Support Loans

An Australian Apprenticeship Support Loan (AASL) is an interest free loan to help you meet day to day costs while undertaking your studies. You can borrow up to $27,048 (2026-2027), which is paid in monthly instalments. You can apply for an AASL i **f you are completing an Australian Apprenticeship in a qualification listed on the** [Australian Apprenticeship Priority List.arrow\_outwardOpens in new window or tab](https://www.dewr.gov.au/australian-apprenticeships/apprenticeship-support#toc-australian-apprenticeship-priority-list)

**You will not have to repay your loan until you are earning an income above the minimum repayment threshold**($69,528 for 2026-27). Indexation of your loan will be capped at the lower of the Wage Price Index or the Consumer Price Index.

**Once you complete your apprenticeship, you will receive a 20% discount on your loan amount.**

To find out more about an AASL, [talk to your Apprentice Connect Australia Provider](https://www.apprenticeships.gov.au/who-to-contact/search-for-a-provider). Your provider will take you (and your parent or guardian, if you’re under 18) through the loan program in detail.

Use the guides below to learn about Australian Apprenticeship Support Loans and how to apply for one using the [Apprenticeships Data Management Systemarrow\_outwardOpens in new window or tab](https://adms.australianapprenticeships.gov.au/adms/sign-in).

**The Australian Government has passed legislation to reduce all student and training support debt.** Australian Apprentices with an outstanding student debt as at 1 June 2025 will have a one-off 20% reduction applied to their student debt. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) has backdated these changes to 1 June 2025 before the annual indexation was applied. This means indexation will only be applied to the lower debt amount.

The Australian Government has also introduced a ‘marginal repayment system’ where compulsory repayments are calculated only on income above the minimum repayment threshold.

For more information on your existing AASL or other student debt, or to view the balance of your loan, visit the ATO app or online services.

## Living Away From Home Allowance

If you have to move away from your parents’ or guardians’ home to start or continue training as an Australian Apprentice, you may be eligible to receive the Living Away From Home Allowance (LAFHA) to help you with cost-of-living pressures.

LAFHA is a weekly tax-free payment that reduces as you progress in your training.

- In your first year of training, you would receive: $125.52 per week
- In your second year of training, you would receive: $94.14 per week
- In your third year of training, you would receive: $47.07 per week

Each year on 1 July, LAFHA rates will be adjusted in line with the March quarter Consumer Price Index (CPI) as published by the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS).

### Am I eligible?

The [Australian Apprenticeships Incentive System Guidelinesarrow\_outwardOpens in new window or tab](https://www.dewr.gov.au/skills-support-individuals/resources/australian-apprenticeships-incentive-system-guidelines) outline the detailed eligibility for the Living Away From Home Allowance. Your [Apprentice Connect Australia Provider](https://www.apprenticeships.gov.au/who-to-contact/search-for-a-provider) is also able to advise you on your eligibility and can help you to lodge a claim in the [Apprenticeships Data Management Systemarrow\_outwardOpens in new window or tab](https://adms.australianapprenticeships.gov.au/adms/sign-in).

## Grandfathered Payments

### Australian Apprenticeships Incentive System Guidelines 1 July 2024 to 31 December 2025

Apprentices and Employers who commenced or recommenced after 1 July 2024 and prior to 31 December 2025 will continue to receive support through the grandfathering arrangements as outlined below.

### Australian Apprentice Training Support Payment

#### What is it?

The Australian Apprentice Training Support Payment is for Australian Apprentices training towards an occupation and qualification at a Certificate level III or above listed on the [Australian Apprenticeships Priority ListOpens in new window or tabarrow\_outwardOpens in new window or tab](https://www.dewr.gov.au/australian-apprenticeships/apprenticeship-support#toc-australian-apprenticeship-priority-list).

This payment is front loaded and paid in four instalments after you start your training.

- $1,750 at 6 and 12 months and $750 at 18 and 24 months for full-time apprentices
- $875 at 6 and 12 months and $375 at 18 and 24 months for part-time apprentices

#### How do I claim it?

Claims are processed through the [Apprenticeships Data Management SystemOpens in new window or tabarrow\_outwardOpens in new window or tab](https://adms.australianapprenticeships.gov.au/adms/sign-in). Your [Apprentice Connect Australia Provider](https://www.apprenticeships.gov.au/who-to-contact/search-for-an-australian-apprenticeship-support-network-provider) can help you with any questions you have about your claim.

### New Energy Apprentice Support Payment

Apprentices who commenced or recommenced prior to 1 July 2025 will continue to receive the support through grandfathering arrangements as below:

- The **New Energy Apprentice Support Payment** provides financial support of up to $10,000 for a full-time apprenticeship and up to $5,000 for a part-time apprenticeship over the life of the Australian Apprenticeship. Payments are made according to the following schedule and rates:
  - $2,000 at 6, 12, 24 and 36 months and on completion (full-time)
  - $1,000 at 6, 12, 24 and 36 months and on completion (part-time)

## Other government payments

In addition to apprenticeship supports, you may be eligible for other general supports on offer from [Services Australiaarrow\_outwardOpens in new window or tab](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/) while training as an apprentice.

These payments may include:

- [Youth Allowancearrow\_outwardOpens in new window or tab](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/youth-allowance) \- Financial help if you’re 24 or younger.
- [Austudyarrow\_outwardOpens in new window or tab](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/austudy) \- Financial help if you're 25 or older.
- [ABSTUDYarrow\_outwardOpens in new window or tab](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/abstudy) \- Payments for Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander apprentices.

To learn more about these payments, [visit the Services Australia websitearrow\_outwardOpens in new window or tab](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/).

### State and Territory Government Support

Your state or territory may offer additional incentives throughout your training. Speak with an Apprentice Connect Australia Provider to learn about what else may be available.
